msg: No USER instruction — the image runs every process as root (uid 0).
fix: Create an unprivileged account and end the build with USER 10001 (a numeric uid survives a re-tagged base image).

msg: USER root — the container runs with uid 0, so a container escape starts as host root.
fix: Drop back to an unprivileged uid after the privileged build steps: USER 10001.

msg: Base image is pinned by tag, not by digest — the bytes you assessed are not the bytes you ship.
Base image uses :latest or no tag — the image contents change without a code change.
fix: Name an immutable version and digest instead of :latest.

msg: Clear-text secret baked into an image layer — it stays readable in the layer even if a later line deletes it.
fix: Mount it at run time (--secret / *_FILE pointing at /run/secrets) and never as ENV or ARG.

msg: ADD pulls an unverified file from the network into the image at build time.
fix: Fetch it in a RUN step, verify a published checksum, then COPY it in.

msg: Certificate checking is switched off for a build-time download.
fix: Remove the flag and install the CA bundle the mirror actually needs.

msg: Plain-text HTTP source — anything on the path can replace what lands in the image.
fix: Use https:// and pin the package or checksum.

msg: Remote script piped straight into a shell — unreviewed code runs with build privileges.
fix: Download, check the signature or checksum, then run the saved file.

msg: sudo inside a container is a privilege-escalation path that the container does not need.
fix: Do privileged work as root before the USER line, then drop; remove the sudo package.

msg: Packages installed without a version pin — two builds of the same commit hold different CVEs.
fix: Pin every package (curl=7.88.1-10+deb12u5) so a scan result stays true for the image you ship.

msg: An SSH daemon inside the container adds a second, unmonitored way in.
fix: Remove it and reach the container with docker exec / kubectl exec, which your audit trail already covers.

msg: privileged: true hands the container every capability and the host device tree.
fix: Delete it and grant only the one capability the workload actually needs.

msg: The Docker socket is mounted into the container — that is equivalent to giving it root on the host.
fix: Use a socket proxy with a read-only allow-list, or move the job to a build runner outside the container.

msg: network_mode: host removes the network boundary between the container and the host.
fix: Use a user-defined bridge network and publish only the ports you mean to publish.

msg: A host namespace is shared with the container, so it can see and signal host processes.
fix: Remove the host namespace setting; keep the container in its own pid/ipc namespace.

msg: A capability that defeats container isolation is added back to the container.
fix: cap_drop: [ALL] first, then add back only the narrow capability you can name a reason for.

msg: Port published on every host interface — it is reachable from outside the boundary, not just from localhost.
Clear-text secret in the compose file — it lands in your repository and in every developer's shell history.
fix: Move it to a compose secret or a *_FILE variable pointing at /run/secrets.
